startup.name: Relling
startup.one_liner: Deploying the first billion robots for manufacturing
startup.description: San Francisco robotics company in Summer 2025 with the stated aim of deploying very large numbers of robots in manufacturing. The input gives no description, team size, product, customers or revenue, so the product form (arms, mobile robots, software or a robot as a service business) is unknown.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up for the hot robotics theme and a San Francisco hardware ambition that fits YC priorities. Neutral on team, since none is stated. Down because a one line pitch of a billion robots has no stated customer or product. Net about 3 percent, conditional on the batch already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say that deploying the first billion robots is a vision and not a wedge, and that hardware manufacturing automation needs capital and long sales cycles that do not fit a three month demo. Without a named customer or a working robot, partners may prefer a founder with prior factory deployments.

Time table era 2022+: seed median 6 months, p75 14.2; series_a p25 19.4, median 28, p75 38.4; series_b median 35.6 from batch start.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16.3 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17 and the number is for a round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchor 0.59 (B2B) and 0.57 (robotics, n=7); 0.50 is 0.85x of the B2B anchor, because about 85 percent of eventual seeds close within 16 months (p75 14.2 months). Robotics enthusiasm in 2025 is not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test, and a vague one line pitch with no known traction gives no reason to. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, the most common outcome for a small team that closes a first outside round quickly.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later YC median of 4.1M, with market pre money near 18M.
Strong seed led by a known fund, matching the upper quartile of 6.5M and above in press covered rounds.
Large hot category round; rare for a team this early.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if the founders cannot show a working robot deployed with a paying factory inside a year, because hardware investors want pilots and not slides. Manufacturing robotics has a record of slow sales cycles and capital needs: Voodoo Manufacturing and Pashi both shut down, and Daedalus took years to a small raise. A team with no disclosed customer or product form may raise only the standard YC deal.

Series A for 2022 and later YC companies has p25 at 19.4 months from batch start, so only a small share of eventual A raisers close inside this window. 0.26 (B2B anchor) times about 0.25 gives 0.065, set at 0.06; robotics tag cohort has 0 of 4 known so no lift.

bands.rationale: Small or slow Series A below the 2022 and later p25 of 10M.
Typical Series A near the 2022 and later YC median of 14.15M and a market deal size near 17M.
Upside round after fast revenue growth; the p75 is about 20M.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 16 months needs repeat factory orders and a path to margins on hardware, which almost no robotics company shows that early. Industrial Next took about three years from its 2022 seed to a Series A, and Autumn Labs has stayed at an unverified small round, so a first deployment story is the usual stopping point.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside 16 months of YC would need a breakout fleet and revenue growth, as seen only for a few humanoid and foundation model robotics leaders. A factory robot startup of unknown size has no analog among Voodoo, Daedalus or Industrial Next that reached B this fast.

anchors.adjustment_reason: No base rate (0 of 3 reached C in the B2B 2022 and later cohort). Placeholder 0.01 for the 16 month window.

bands.rationale: Smaller later round near the 2022 and later p25 of 35M (n=9 only).
Typical Series C or later, 45M to 77M per the YC table and market monitor.
Breakout late round at unicorn scale; very rare in this cohort.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C within 16 months would need category leading scale in robot deployments. Even well funded industrial robotics founders took four or more years to get there, and none of the analogs did, so the odds are near zero in this window and a stated plan for a billion robots would have to be reduced to a first fleet before any later round is plausible.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stalls at the pilot stage or sells to a larger automation firm for a small sum, as Voodoo Manufacturing and Pashi ended in shutdown. The upside needs a standardized robot cell sold repeatedly, where well funded humanoid and cell makers are competing for the same factory budgets.

AI for manufacturing from factory veterans.

killers.evidence: The input gives only a vision statement. Industrial robot buyers want a pilot with a defined task, and the market search lists welding, sanding, assembly and machine loading as the funded tasks.
killers.mitigation: Pick one factory task and sign one paying pilot.

killers.evidence: Robots need prototypes, safety certification and field service before revenue, and trackers say robotics money concentrates in a few large rounds.
killers.mitigation: Sell robots as a service on a small fleet and use pilot revenue.

killers.risk: Better funded robotics and humanoid players
killers.evidence: Trackers report the top 10 robotics startups take about half of disclosed funding.
killers.mitigation: Focus on a vertical the large players ignore.

killers.evidence: Factories evaluate for months and Industrial Next needed years to reach a Series A.
killers.mitigation: Target small and mid size shops with faster buying.

competition_now.name: Industrial robot arm makers and integrators
competition_now.what: Established vendors selling arms and cells to factories

competition_now.name: Funded robotics startups for welding, sanding and assembly
competition_now.traction: Top 10 hold about half of disclosed funding per trackers

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable robots in real factories need perception, grasping, safety and integration with existing lines. A small team can show a cell in months but production grade uptime takes years, and that is the moat if solved. The input does not say which part is built.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large arm makers and funded humanoid companies could enter any broad factory task, but a narrow vertical integration takes time. A billion robots framing overlaps with the best funded players.

evidence.claim: Robotics investment recovered in 2025 and industrial startups target welding, fastening and handling tasks that factories pay for.
Robots as a service and modular automation are reducing the capital hurdle for smaller manufacturers.

roadmap.goal: Show one real factory task automated.
actions: Pick a single task such as machine loading
Run a paid pilot at one plant
roadmap.proof: One customer paying monthly for a running robot.

roadmap.goal: Repeat the pilot at three or more sites.
actions: Price as robots as a service
roadmap.proof: Three paying sites with robots running above 90 percent uptime.

pros.evidence: Industrial robotics funding rebounded after 2025 per public trackers.
Manufacturers already spend on automation and labour shortages push demand for robots.

brand.rationale: An invented two syllable name is common among industrial startups and carries neither meaning nor harm; unlike a descriptive name it needs the product to build its recall, as with Daedalus.

narrative.headline: A grand robotics vision with no stated product or customer: seed is a little better than a coin flip over 16 months, later rounds are unlikely in the window.
narrative.general_summary: Relling states the aim of deploying the first billion robots in manufacturing, and the input offers no product, team or traction. The window is 16.3 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17, long enough for most seeds, so seed sits at 0.50 against anchors of 0.57 to 0.59. Series A given seed is 0.06 in the window. The odds do not rank this company against others, and the robotics boom is not credited beyond the anchor.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2025-07-07 using only the input.
Seed means above about 1M from outside investors inside the 16.3 month window.
Team size and product form are unknown and no traction is assumed.
